summary: Implements the eight file operations: parse, inspect_schema, write, copy, stream, parse_bytes, inspect_schema_bytes and serialise_bytes. It resolves path templates, globs, archives, storage and auth profiles, location policy and transform pipelines, routes each read to a byte, random-access or sequential transport handle, normalises tabular output and checks append schemas.
lifecycle_notes: Formats resolve before any I/O, so an unknown suffix raises without touching storage.
A source with a glob expands into one child source per matched path and recurses with glob=None.
Archive reads disable suffix inference unless source.infer is set, then extract members and resolve each member's format separately.
Append reads the destination, requires identical ordered names and types, unions nullability, keeps the destination's metadata and rewrites the whole object.
_with_access falls back to whole-object bytes when transforms apply or the backend refuses ranged or streamed access.
documentation_hooks: Read path: template, glob, archive, format, access mode
Schema discovery: metadata, full and bounded bases
risks: Append rewrites the whole object: cost grows with the destination size, and nothing coordinates concurrent appends.
_normalise_output is the single tabular-normalisation seam. Changing it affects every format's output= behaviour.
_read_source carries archive, glob and non-archive branches in one function, so the three paths can drift apart.
